istem: Muffled winter storm heard from inside a closed stone village house at night. Low, dull, broadband wind rush through thick walls, soft gusts slowly swelling and fading, a heavy wooden door gently pressing in its frame, distant snow-laden gusts sweeping across the roof. Dark, warm, noise-like room tone, no melody.
A single very soft fingertip tap on a thick leather-bound book cover. Muted, dry, close, gentle, extremely short.
A single soft touch of a fingertip on thick handmade paper, a tiny muted papery tap. Dry, close, gentle, extremely short.
Turning one heavy parchment page of an old manuscript book: a thick paper flip with a soft papery swish, ending with a light muted knock of wood on a wooden table. Close, dry, warm.
Turning one heavy parchment page of an old manuscript book: a thick paper flip with a soft papery swish, ending with a light muted knock of wood on a wooden table. Close, dry, warm.
Turning one heavy parchment page of an old manuscript book: a thick paper flip with a soft papery swish, ending with a light muted knock of wood on a wooden table. Close, dry, warm.
A single gentle page turn of an old paper book, crisp soft paper flip. Close, dry, quiet room.
A single gentle page turn of an old paper book, crisp soft paper flip. Close, dry, quiet room.

Low steady breath of a small hearth fire inside a quiet stone village house at night: soft continuous flame rustle, warm room tone, very faint wind far outside, only tiny sparse crackles. Calm, intimate, no voices, no music.
Warm summer breeze moving through tall dry grass in an open Anatolian meadow: soft continuous rustling, wide open air, calm and spacious. No birds, no insects, no voices, no music.

A medieval Anatolian bazaar street with stone paving: low murmur of a distant crowd with indistinct voices and no clear words, shuffling footsteps on stone, faint wooden cart wheels far away, open-air echo between stone walls. No engines, no vehicles, no music, no modern sounds.
A short burst of wood fire crackling in a stone hearth: a few sharp ember pops and snaps, close, warm quiet room.
A burning log shifting and settling in a hearth: soft wooden crunch, a small collapse of glowing embers and a brief hiss of sparks.
A skylark singing briefly high above an open summer field, distant and airy, natural outdoor recording.
A short burst of grasshopper chirping in dry summer grass nearby, then it stops.
A coppersmith tapping a small hammer on a copper pot a few times inside a workshop, heard from a medieval stone bazaar street.
A donkey braying once in the distance in an old stone market street, natural outdoor recording.

istem: [thoughtful] The year 1243… [short pause] At the Battle of Köse Dağ, which changed the fate of Anatolia, the Seljuk army suffered a crushing defeat.

ayarlar.next_text: [sighs] In its wake, Mongol raids spread to every corner of Anatolia. Cities were plundered; villages stood empty. [sad] Beneath a shifting order and ever heavier taxes, the people struggled to survive. [calm] Still, the caravans kept to their roads. People tried not to lose hope. [whisper] For in Anatolia there was an old saying: [long pause] The ash keeps the ember.

istem: [thoughtful] Año 1243… [short pause] En la batalla de Köse Dağ, que cambió el destino de Anatolia, el ejército selyúcida sufrió una dura derrota.

ayarlar.next_text: [sighs] Tras aquella derrota, las incursiones mongolas se extendieron por toda Anatolia. Las ciudades fueron saqueadas; las aldeas quedaron vacías. [sad] Bajo un orden que cambiaba y tributos cada vez más pesados, el pueblo luchó por sobrevivir. [calm] Aun así, las caravanas siguieron su camino. La gente intentó no perder la esperanza. [whisper] Porque en Anatolia había un viejo dicho: [long pause] La ceniza guarda la brasa.

istem: [thoughtful] Ano de 1243… [short pause] Na Batalha de Köse Dağ, que mudou o destino da Anatólia, o exército seljúcida sofreu uma dura derrota.

ayarlar.next_text: [sighs] Depois dessa derrota, as incursões mongóis se espalharam por todos os cantos da Anatólia. Cidades foram saqueadas; aldeias ficaram vazias. [sad] Sob uma ordem que mudava e impostos cada vez mais pesados, o povo lutou para sobreviver. [calm] Ainda assim, as caravanas seguiram seu caminho. As pessoas tentaram não perder a esperança. [whisper] Porque na Anatólia havia um velho ditado: [long pause] A cinza guarda a brasa.

istem: [thoughtful] عامُ ألفٍ ومئتين وثلاثةٍ وأربعين للميلاد… [short pause] في معركة كوسه داغ، التي غيّرت مصير الأناضول، مُني الجيشُ السلجوقيُّ بهزيمةٍ قاسية.

ayarlar.next_text: [sighs] وفي أعقاب تلك الهزيمة، اجتاحت غاراتُ المغول أرجاءَ الأناضول كلَّها. نُهبت المدن، وخلت القرى من أهلها. [sad] وتحت نظامٍ يتبدّل وضرائبَ تزداد ثقلًا، كافح الناسُ من أجل البقاء. [calm] ومع ذلك، مضت القوافلُ في طرقها، وحاول الناسُ ألّا يفقدوا الأمل. [whisper] فقد كان في الأناضول قولٌ قديم: [long pause] الرمادُ يحفظُ الجمر.

istem: [thoughtful] Тысяча двести сорок третий год… [short pause] В битве при Кёсе-Даге, изменившей судьбу Анатолии, сельджукское войско потерпело тяжёлое поражение.

ayarlar.next_text: [sighs] Вслед за этим монгольские набеги прокатились по всей Анатолии. Города были разграблены, деревни опустели. [sad] Под гнётом нового порядка и всё более тяжёлых податей люди боролись за жизнь. [calm] И всё же караваны продолжали свой путь. Люди старались не терять надежды. [whisper] Ведь в Анатолии издавна говорили: [long pause] Пепел хранит жар.
